permutationLabel: Post-operative day 3, oliguric AKI stage 3, nephrotoxins
summary: 66-year-old woman, day 3 after Hartmann's procedure, oliguric; creatinine 268 (baseline 78), K 6.7 with peaked T waves, on gentamicin, ibuprofen and ramipril.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Low urine output after bowel operation
inputs.hpi: Day 3 after emergency Hartmann's procedure for perforated sigmoid diverticulitis. Urine output 15 mL/h for the last 8 hours. Received gentamicin for 3 days, ibuprofen PRN on the ward, and ramipril was restarted yesterday. Feels weak. No chest pain.

exam.general: Alert. Pulse 104/min, BP 104/58, RR 20, temperature 37.6°C, SpO2 95% on air. Mild peripheral oedema.
exam.abdomen: Midline wound clean, stoma pink and working. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender around the wound. Catheter in situ draining concentrated urine.
exam.cardiovascular: ECG: peaked T waves, QRS 96 ms, sinus rhythm.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Post-operative AKI (KDIGO stage 3) with severe hyperkalaemia
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Oliguric AKI stage 3 (creatinine 268 from 78) after emergency laparotomy, nephrotoxins (gentamicin, ibuprofen, ramipril); potassium 6.7 with peaked T waves.

guideline.name: UK Kidney Association — Clinical practice guideline: treatment of acute hyperkalaemia in adults
guideline.section: Severity (mild 5.5–5.9, moderate 6.0–6.4, severe ≥6.5 mmol/L); urgent 12-lead ECG and cardiac monitoring; IV calcium (calcium chloride 10% 10 mL or calcium gluconate 10% 30 mL) for ECG changes; insulin–glucose (10 units soluble insulin with 25 g glucose) with glucose monitoring to prevent hypoglycaemia; nebulised salbutamol as adjunct; stop/withhold drugs that raise potassium; treat the cause; dialysis for refractory hyperkalaemia
guideline.citation: UK Kidney Association. Clinical Practice Guidelines: Treatment of Acute Hyperkalaemia in Adults. UKKA; 2023 (update of the 2020 Renal Association guideline).

guideline.name: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury
guideline.section: 2.1 Definition and staging (creatinine rise ≥26.5 µmol/L in 48 h or ≥1.5× baseline in 7 days, or urine output <0.5 mL/kg/h for 6 h; stage by creatinine ratio/urine output); 3.1 fluids and haemodynamic management; discontinue nephrotoxic agents; evaluate cause
guideline.citation: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Acute Kidney Injury Work Group. KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury. Kidney Int Suppl. 2012;2:1–138.

guideline.name: NICE NG148 — Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management
guideline.section: Detection (creatinine against baseline); urinalysis for all with AKI; ultrasound of the urinary tract within 24 h when obstruction is suspected (immediately if pyonephrosis suspected); stop/withhold nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics) and review metformin; refer to urology immediately for pyonephrosis, obstructed solitary kidney, bilateral upper tract obstruction or complications of obstruction; nephrology referral criteria
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management. NICE guideline NG148. London: NICE; 2019.

rationale: Surgical AKI with severe hyperkalaemia: UKKA emergency treatment plus NICE NG148 nephrotoxin withdrawal.
